recommendation_summary: Action now: the reply rejects the initials column and naming convention. Instead, a reviewer who did not write the document copies the exact released file into a retention folder that authors cannot modify, on storage already kept for seven years, and sets that copy read-only. The reviewer then adds the checksum, author, approver account and approval time to a reviewer-only log stored with the copy. The agent offers to set this up once the user names the share. Optional additions: none. Unmet needs: the user must choose the share; the folder and contract have not been inspected; separation of author and approver relies on reviewer-only access and the procedure, not on a system check.

labels.Requirements and who asked: The signed customer contract requires every released document to retain its exact approved version, the approver's identity, and the approval time for seven years; authors must not approve their own documents, and later edits must not change the retained version. You asked to keep the shared folder, add an APPROVED column of typed initials, and agree a naming convention for this week's delivery.
labels.Deleted: Typed initials and a naming convention as the control, because authors can change both and neither records an authenticated approver or an approval time. A new document system, because one read-only copy and a reviewer-only log meet the contract.
labels.Bottleneck: Authors can edit the shared folder, so the released file and any approval mark in it can change after release.
labels.Checked myself: What you told me about the contract, the twelve remote authors, the three reviewers, weekly releases, and author edit access to the current folder. I have not inspected the folder or the contract.

note: The reply chooses an access-controlled, read-only retention copy with a checksum-bound, reviewer-only approval log kept for seven years, which meets the LARGER capabilities.
